newsitem.title: CHILE: Quebrada Blanca Feb copper output hurt by rain.
newsitem.headline: Quebrada Blanca Feb copper output hurt by rain.

text.p: Chile's Quebrada Blanca mine said its February copper output was lower than expected due to heavy rainfall in the northern Atacama Desert which damaged access roads and slowed the pit's heap-leaching process.

The mine, which lies high in the Andes near the border with Bolivia, produced 4,633 tonnes of copper cathodes in February compared with planned production of 6,000 tonnes, said general manager James Drake.
"We were short in the month, not for technical problems but because of the dilution effect of the rainfall," Drake told Reuters.
Rain diluted the copper-rich acid solution flowing from the mine's huge leach pads which sprawl across a hillside near the heap-leaching plant, he said.
Vancouver-based Cominco Ltd, Cominco Resources and Teck Resources International hold a 76.5 percent stake in Quebrada Blanca, one of the most remote copper pits in Chile.
Chile's arid northern highlands, among the driest spots in the world, have been hit this year by rain and floods as the result of unusually severe weather moving across from Bolivia.
Over 70 milliliters of rain fell at Quebrada Blanca in February against an average six milliliters over the last four years, said Drake.
The mine had to suspend operations temporarily last month as the rain made roads slippery and lightening storms came close to the pit, he said.
Quebrada Blanca produced 68,000 tonnes of copper in 1996 and expects to reach design capacity of 75,000 tonnes this year.
